cue.purpose: Largest type on a page: the live release number (mono) and the sign-in wordmark.

title.purpose: Project name beside its spike strip; desk wordmark.

body.purpose: Running text, table cells, controls; 600 for buttons, 700 for sheet headings.

meta.purpose: Labels, hints, table headers, timestamps, small buttons.

mono.purpose: Anything typed or copied: commands, logs, env keys, hostnames. Same meta size; mono also runs at body and cue sizes.

motion.name: transition-colors
motion.purpose: All hover and state colour changes.

motion.name: lamp-go
motion.purpose: Go lamp lands on the newly live row; the one authored moment.

motion.name: lamp-standby
motion.purpose: Standby ring blink while armed or running.

motion.name: standby-timeout
motion.purpose: Armed standby-then-go stands down after this.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Both lamp animations stop under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
Every release is a cue in a stage manager's prompt book: it stands by until it proves itself, then goes, and the previous one bows out. The interface is a running-light blue prompt-desk bar over a cool rehearsal-floor grey. The work sits on white sheets, cue lamps report state, and a short strip of spike tape marks each project.

The system is dense, quiet and data-first. One workhorse family in two widths (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Mono) carries everything at four sizes. Colour is scarce. Blue belongs to the desk, the primary action and the single reversed plate. Green, amber and red belong to the lamps and their ink. The fluorescent tape colours appear only on spike strips. Depth comes from rules and the sheet-on-floor contrast, never from shadows.

Motion is limited to one authored moment: the go lamp landing on its new row when a release hands over. Everything else is a 150 ms colour transition.
keyCharacteristics: A blue desk bar on top, a grey floor below, white sheets for primary work, and ruled quiet sections for supporting work.
Cue lamps whose state reads from shape as well as colour.
Spike-tape strips derived from the project name.
Four type sizes, two widths of one family.
A two-press standby-then-go call before any action that changes what is live or deletes configuration.

rules.name: The Lamp Colour Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red mean live, standby and failed. They are never used to decorate.

rules.name: The Neutral Ground Rule
rules.body: In dark mode the blue stays on the desk and the plate. The floor, sheets and rules are neutral greys.

rules.name: The Tape Is Identity Rule
rules.body: Fluorescent tape colours appear only on spike strips. They never carry state.

rules.name: The Four Sizes Rule
rules.body: There are exactly four type sizes: meta, body, title and cue. Express hierarchy through weight (400/600/700) and the mono width, never through a fifth size.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every label, heading and button uses plain sentence case, with no uppercase tracking. A heading names its sheet and nothing restates it.

rules.name: The Ruled Not Raised Rule
rules.body: Separate surfaces with 1px rules and the sheet-against-floor contrast. Do not add box-shadows.

rules.name: The One Plate Rule
rules.body: The live release row is the only reversed row in the interface. The selected tab of the log service switcher uses the same plate colour as a selection state, but no other row or card is ever reversed.

dos: **Do** mark every project with its spike strip, using the colour derived from the name.
**Do** carry lamp state through shape as well as colour (filled, ringed, struck, hollow, grey disc).
**Do** gate roll back, redeploy and env/domain deletion behind standby-then-go, with a go label that names the exact outcome.
**Do** put primary work on full sheets and supporting work in quiet sections on the floor.
**Do** set anything a user types or copies in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono.
**Do** keep transitions to 150 ms colour changes and respect reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** reverse any row other than the live release.
**Don't** use box-shadows; separate surfaces with 1px rules.
**Don't** put blue on the floor or the sheets in dark mode; keep blue on the desk, plate and action.
**Don't** use lamp green, amber or red, or spike-tape colours, for decoration.
**Don't** use a dark sidebar with a grid of project cards; projects are a ruled list on a sheet.
